QUESTION:
The absolute refractory period during an action potential generation is primarily caused by:

(A) Closure of voltage-gated K^+ channels.
(B) Inactivation of voltage-gated Na^+channels.
(C) Increased permeability to Cl^−ions.
(D) Continuous activation of the Na^+/K^+pump.

STORED ANSWER KEY: "B"

STORED SOLUTION:
The absolute refractory period is the short interval immediately following the generation of an action potential during which the neuron is completely incapable of generating another action potential, regardless of the strength of the stimulus. This period is primarily due to the inactivation of the voltage-gated Na+channels. Although the membrane is depolarized (which would normally open them), these specific channels enter a temporary, locked inactivated state that prevents them from opening again, thereby halting the influx of Na+ ions required for a new depolarization.
